intent.name: exam.mark.set
intent.summary: Record one student's score for a subject in an exam. One step, and every figure is the teacher's.

routesElsewhere.note: Grace is a separate award with its own limits, and a pass achieved on it is recorded as such (BR-7).

plan.atomicity: One write: the mark and the audit entry together or not at all. Entering a mark produces no grade — grading is calculated separately from the bands the teacher defined (BR-13), so nothing is visible to a family from this.

planningRules.rule: Never supply a score the actor did not state. It is a child's result, read by their family and carried into every grade and average that follows — a figure a planner produced is a mark nobody awarded.
Never record a zero for an absent student. Absent is a state on the mark, not a score, and the two are treated differently by grade calculation (BR-8, UC-06-03 BR-4).
Never round or cap a score to fit the total. E1 is BR-2 working — report the total and let the teacher say what the mark actually is.

Never add grace as part of setting a mark. Grace has its own limits, its own refusals and its own record on the result (BR-4 to BR-7), and a score quietly raised to a pass hides something the school decided.
Report the shortfall where the score is below the pass mark. It is what grace is measured against (BR-4), and the teacher deciding whether to award it needs the figure.
Report how many students still carry no entry. The sheet cannot be submitted while any is blank, and a blank is not a mark (BR-3, E7).
Never describe a mark as producing a grade. Entering marks produces no grade; grading is calculated separately (BR-13).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Before submission a mark is simply set again. After submission only the Coordinator changes it, with a reason and the previous value kept (BR-10); after the lock nothing changes without the exam being reopened (BR-11).

planningRules.rule: Never raise the score instead of awarding grace. The result shows that a pass was by grace and how many marks were given (BR-7) — a score quietly lifted to the pass mark hides a decision the school made about a child.

Never compute the shortfall in the plan. Where the actor asked to bring a student up to the pass mark, omit the figure and let the API award exactly what is needed — a planner's arithmetic on somebody's result is a mark nobody checked.

planningRules.rule: Never lock as a step after submitting. Submission is the teacher's act and the lock is the School Admin's, and between them sits the Coordinator's correction window (BR-8, BR-10) — a chained lock closes that window before anybody has looked.
Never confuse this with the result lock. This freezes the raw number so the grade is computed on something stable; the other freezes what was published (BR-8).
Say plainly what the lock closes. No change is possible afterwards without the exam being reopened (BR-11), which is deliberate and visible.
Never describe locking as publishing. Nothing reaches a student or a family from it (UC-06-03 BR-6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Reopening the marks, which is a separate and deliberate act carrying a reason (BR-11). It is never chained onto a refusal.

routesElsewhere.note: A correction is refused while the marks are locked (E10). Reopening comes first, deliberately and on its own.

routesElsewhere.note: The two locks are separate, and so are the two reopenings (BR-8).

steps.note: One step, and only this step. The correction that follows is the Coordinator's separate act, and the relock is the School Admin's (BR-11, A6).

plan.atomicity: One write: the reopening, its reason and the audit entry together or not at all. The marks become changeable by the Coordinator again. Where a result had been released from these marks, correcting one recalculates the grade by the same bands and republishes it with the change visible (UC-06-03 BR-10, BR-12).

operations.name: exam.marks.reopen
operations.idempotencyKey: exam_id + class_id + subject_id, since a sheet is reopened once per lock
operations.purpose: Reopen a locked marks sheet so corrections can be made.

parameters.name: exam_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No exam matches within the actor's scope for this session.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their code and dates.

parameters.notes: The exam the paper belongs to.

parameters.name: class_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No class matches within the actor's scope.

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the subjects in the exam and their status.

parameters.notes: The subject whose marks are being frozen or reopened.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Why a locked sheet is being reopened. This is the record of a deliberate act, so it says what was found wrong.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

errors.meaning: The marks are not locked.
errors.note: There is nothing to reopen; the Coordinator can already correct them.

errors.meaning: A reopening was recorded with no reason.

planningRules.rule: Never chain a reopening onto a refused correction. The lock exists so that changing a final mark is a deliberate act by a different person (BR-11) — a plan that reopened, corrected and relocked in one breath would make the lock decorative.
Never compose the reason. It is the record of why final marks were unfrozen, and it is read long afterwards by whoever asks how a result changed.
Report where a result was already released from these marks. A correction will recalculate the grade and republish it with the change visible, and families will see it (UC-06-03 BR-12).
Never relock in the same plan. The correction has to happen in between, and it is the Coordinator's (A6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Locking the marks again, after the correction has been made. That is the School Admin's separate act and never part of this plan.
